EVIDENCE (all falsifiable, all bound to the real /api/user/search path driven from inside the window):
- INVOCATION: sidecar CPU delta measured across a SINGLE request = 4170ms CPU / ~1.3s wall (~3.2 ORT threads). Rerank is genuinely called on the user-facing path, not bypassed.
- ORDERING CHANGES: 3 of 4 queries returned hits whose RRF `rank` is NOT monotonically descending — a lower-RRF hit was promoted above a higher-RRF one, which only the cross-encoder can cause. The 4th query is the documented single-bucket case where the qualityScore tiebreak deliberately preserves RRF order.
- LATENCY: 24 candidates = 1316ms (54.9 ms/pair), reproducing P-009's 52 ms/pair and comfortably inside PROSE_RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS (4000ms). Whole search 3.4-4.5s end-to-end at box load ~96.

Two verification traps worth carrying: (1) `rank` in the /api/user/search response is the RRF score carried through untouched, NOT the rerank score, so it can never be used to check rerank ordering directly; test RRF-monotonicity instead. (2) Recomputing rerank scores externally cannot settle ordering — bucketing is round(score*20), so a 0.9026 lands in bucket 18 while 19 needs >=0.925, and any small text-reconstruction difference flips the bucket. rows.nowState: FIX LANDED + GREEN. Root cause was an INVERTED TIMEOUT HIERARCHY, not a hang: measured opus at 62.4 tok/s => a full 4096-tok ideator response is ~66s vs a 180s cap (2.7x headroom), so the ideator CANNOT time out by generating. It was blocked in governor.acquire() waiting out a shared rate-limit pause (live depths 15s/120s/453s) and guillotined by an outer timer, then misreported as transport death ($0 spent, 0 ideas). One constant conflated time-to-GENERATE with time-waiting-for-CAPACITY. FIXED by separating the ADMISSION budget from the GENERATION budget: generation timer starts on admission (new onAdmitted seam), admission bounded by the cycle deadline (propagated scheduler->runner->cycle->ideators; the cycle recordingLlm wrapper bounds EVERY in-cycle call so no port can forget). All additive: no deadline => byte-identical old behavior. Guards: ideators 29/29 (5 new, incl. one that pins THE BUG: an admission wait longer than the generation cap must still succeed). tsc clean on all touched files. Also greened a live tsc red in scheduler.ts (reason union missing "no-capacity"). CORROBORATED by f69a7 WI-4541/4542 (gateway serialized the whole fleet through ONE admission slot; tiers ~inert) — that is WHY admission waits got long enough to blow the axe; their fix cuts the magnitude, mine stops the misreport + the cycle-eating.

rows.nowState:
NEW [owner:Avi 2026-07-11]. Owner killed a fleet by closing its terminals; the killed members' work-item leases (work_items.taken_by) were NOT released — persisted for the 6-day lease TTL, poisoning items for any successor. Owner directive (verbatim): "shouldn't our system have automatically unclaimed it as soon as I killed them... it shouldn't have to unclaim on a poll, it should be able to be done on a trigger when I close the console by listening to some event... We want a check to happen on a schedule too in case the event isn't fired for some reason, but it's better to get notified as soon as the console/session terminates."

**Root cause (grounded):** (1) the presence reaper detects a dead session on a ~10-min idle poll but does NOT cascade to release that owner's leases; (2) the SessionEnd/Stop hook already FIRES on every psu session (hooks/cc/lifecycle-report.sh) but only posts a cosmetic activity marker; (3) work_items:release WITHOUT force:true returns ok:true while NOT clearing taken_by (should be not_holder); WITH force:true it DOES clear taken_by (verified on WI-4070). Release mechanism already exists — nothing invokes it on death, and non-force lies about success. See EI-9807 + EI-9808.

**Objective:** Preserve the healthy 30-minute admission safety path, make run reporting truthful, make historical bulk dedup resumable, and measure duplicate-removal quality directly.

**Scope:** admission ledger/reporting; census and ratchet attribution; bulk-stage execution; delta sweep and daily digest reliability; fail-open review debt; durable-park metadata; tests, staging canaries, and runbooks.

**Out of scope:** enabling/disabling/rearming/retuning learning loops; clearing parks by age or parker death; unrelated queue cleanup; force-deploying past a red gate.

**Audit baseline (papercusp-workspace / papercusp, 2026-08-31):**

| Run family | Rows | Writer-recorded result | Effect |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Promoter ticks | 387 | 173 promoter complete, 20 promoter failed, 194 fail-open complete | 440 normal admissions, 13 confirmed merges, 178 fail-open admissions |
| Bulk stages | 8 | 2 complete, 5 failed, 1 running | 3,270 judged pairs in completed stages; 0 merges; 60 holds |

| Delta sweeps | 106 | 88 complete, 18 failed | 43 umbrellas, 144 source links |
| Daily digests | 14 | 2 complete, 5 blocked, 7 failed | 36 umbrellas, 480 links across successful runs |
| Durable-park audits | 11 | 10 report-only complete, 1 explicit reconcile complete | Latest audit saw 1,922 parks; reconcile promoted 20 |

The normal admission path was healthy at measurement: one pending item, about 11 minutes old; 453 promoter-admitted, 167 fail-open unreviewed, and 560 filing-time auto rows. The 1,902 adjudications were 14 r-finding-merge, 1,730 r-related, 154 distinct, and 4 r-remedy-keep.

The final successful bulk stage reviewed 1,500 pairs, all r-related, and merged none. Its census movement from 20,645 to 18,789 is not proof that 1,856 duplicates were removed. The durable-park held total of 6,952 is a sum of repeated snapshots, not a unique-row count.

**Target outcome:** an audit can answer from the ledger which runs completed, failed, blocked, or remain running; which unique rows/pairs changed; what was rolled back; why a run stopped; and whether confirmed merges meet a quality threshold.

rows.reason: The plan has no executable plan items or linked work.
rows.recommendation: Supersede unless a current owner writes executable items and explicitly re-approves the scope.
rows.nowState:
**draft stub.** Carved out from the `papercusp-dogfood-v5`
arc (addendum 2) after the question "how do you prevent token-spend
stats from being faked?" surfaced a broader truth: **anything an
engineer's local operator claims about an LLM call** (spend, latency,
model choice, call count, success rate, refusal rate, throttling) is
structurally self-asserted and cross-engineer-unverifiable — *unless*
every operator routes through a shared witness. The team already has
that witness in the form of the Claude Bridge / Meridian proxy. This
is the plan for turning the proxy from a routing convenience into a
cryptographic source of truth for LLM-side facts.

Spend-witness is the motivating use case (deferred from dogfood-v5
per its addendum 2; v5 currently ships spend as `self-reported` ⏱ tier-D
on the Insights "Spend" card); the pattern is wider.

**Next action:** pick this up after dogfood-v5 ships its non-spend
collaboration layer. First concrete step when picked up: decide
whether the proxy gets a small first-class API for signed
reconciliation feeds, or whether the proxy just commits signed JSON
into shared-harness GIT buckets via a side-channel. Then one
end-to-end spike on spend to validate the substrate before adding
more `kind`s.

Two root causes worth carrying forward, both corrected by probing rather than reading config: (a) PG saturation was NOT PgBouncer — pgbouncer measured healthy (253 clients → 136 backends, cl_waiting=0, maxwait=0). It was postgres-js defaulting idle_timeout to 0 (= never close) in ~13 hand-rolled pools that bypass buildClient. A guard test now fails the build if a pool spreading either shared connection-option helper leaves idle_timeout implicit. (b) Swarm fairness could NOT be built on hyperswarm's peerInfo.topics — that is populated only on the client/lookup path, so INBOUND peers carry an empty topic list and any count on it under-reads inbound-heavy topics. It uses contentPeerCountForTopic instead (announce-channel pairing is symmetric), engages only above 85% budget pressure, and never evicts an established peer.

Still open and unrelated to this plan: WI-6062 (an UNLABELED postgres.js pool holding 5 connections idle for 6.65 days).
